newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda security forces clash with gang - radio.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda security forces clash with gang - radio.

text.p: Rwandan security forces have killed four members of an armed gang in a clash in troubled northwestern Rwanda, state radio said.
It said four members of the gang, trying to hide in a house in Kisaho commune in the northwest province of Ruhengeri, were arrested and 10 escaped in the clash on Thursday night with security forces.
State radio, which was monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said on Friday the gang was believed to have come from a forest on Rwanda's northwestern border with Zaire and Uganda.
The radio earlier this week said eight people were killed and five kidnapped in two attacks by armed groups in Ruhengeri province. An army spokesman said troops were searching for the attackers.
Attacks by Hutu rebels have increased in the northwest since the return of Hutu former militiamen and troops among 600,000 Rwandan refugees who trekked home from eastern Zaire late last year.
The radio also said a tribunal in the southern city of Butare sentenced on Friday two men to death for their part in Rwanda's genocide in 1994 and sentenced a third to five years imprisonment.
It identified the two condemned to death as Edouard Nyipegika and Jean Habimana.

Since December, tribunals across the country have been judging suspects charged with involvement in the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates. Death is the maximum penalty in Rwanda but no one has yet been executed.
Sunday is the third anniversary of the start of the genocide by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs, triggered by the killing of Rwanda's Hutu president when his plane was downed by an explosion.
Human rights groups say the Tutsi-led army this year has killed hundreds of people in the northwest in reprisal for Hutu attacks. The government says some civilians were caught in cross-fire.
